newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish tribunal to probe payments to politicians.
newsitem.headline: Irish tribunal to probe payments to politicians.

text.p: The Irish parliament on Thursday set up a tribunal to investigate alleged payments to politicians by a department store millionaire in a scandal that forced one cabinet minister to resign last year.

Prime Minister John Bruton pledged that "everything will be done to remove the tarnish from the political process" caused by media allegations that politicians had been given money by Ben Dunne, whose family owns an Irish department store chain.
He said the tribunal would ensure "that if there is any evidence of impropriety, it will be dealt with in the appropriate way, in accordance with the laws of the land".
Bertie Ahern, leader of the opposition Fianna Fail party, said the affair was "the biggest political scandal of a financial kind in the history of the state".
The tribunal will start work within the next two weeks in what will be a critical test for all political parties in an election year, political sources said.
Bruton's party and its junior coalition ally, the Labour party, have both said they received money from Dunne for election expenses but denied any wrongdoing.

The tribunal's brief will be to establish whether or not Ireland's political establishment received money from Dunne and why. The affair has raised calls for an overhaul of how Irish political parties are funded.
Michael Lowry, a rising star in Bruton's Fine Gael party, was forced to resign last year after admitting that Dunne paid him 2,000 Irish pounds ($3,200) for the renovation of his private home.
He denied any wrongdoing. He owns a refrigeration business that is used by the Dunnes Stores chain, which has outlets in most Irish high streets.
The media said a very senior politician in the opposition Fianna Fail party had received more than a million pounds from the same source for unspecified purposes.
Charles Haughey, who was Irish Prime Minister for a decade, denied he had received any such sum.
An investigation ordered by Bruton failed to turn up any evidence of major payments to political figures but it failed to ease pressure on his government to investigate the media allegations.
An election is due by November this year but most political experts believe it will be held by June in the wake of the biggest give-away budget in Irish history. ($ = 0.624 Irish Pounds)
